title: Lech Lecha Rashi 5

chapters.title: Avraham's concern for offspring
chapters.about: Avraham questions Hashem about his inheritance and lack of children.

chapters.title: Stepping outside the Mazal
chapters.about: Rashi's explanation of Avraham looking at the stars and changing his name.

chapters.title: Believing in Hashem
chapters.about: Avraham's faith and the distinction between his reaction to the promise of children versus the land.

chapters.title: The animals of the Brit
chapters.about: The specific animals requested for the covenant and their connection to Korbanot.

chapters.title: The covenant process
chapters.about: The meaning of cutting the animals and the appearance of the Shekhinah.

chapters.title: The vultures and the carcasses
chapters.about: Rashi's commentary on the vultures and the symbolic destruction of nations.

summary: Rabbi Soffer explores the dialogue between Avraham Abinu and Hashem regarding the promise of offspring and the inheritance of the land in Parashat Lech Lecha. He examines Rashi's commentary on the Brit Ben HaBetarim, specifically the symbolism of the animals used in the covenant and the significance of the vultures descending on the carcasses.
questions: Why did Hashem tell Avraham to step outside to look at the stars?
Why did Avraham ask for a sign regarding the inheritance of the land but not regarding the promise of children?
What is the symbolic meaning of the animals used in the Brit Ben HaBetarim?
Why did Avraham chase the vultures away from the carcasses?
What does the vulture represent in the context of the nations?
